extracted.intended_audience: ALSC award committee members and chairs (Randolph Caldecott Medal selection)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evaluative guidance for members of the Randolph Caldecott Medal Committee to identify eligible titles and select the most distinguished American picture book for children published in the preceding year, including eligibility, selection criteria, confidentiality, conflict-of-interest, and meeting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / Committee function statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Caldecott Committee is to select the most distinguished American picture book for children, in English, from among those published during the preceding year—within the terms, definitions, and criteria governing the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the primary evaluative aim: identify the single most distinguished American picture book (illustrator receives the Medal); Honor books may be named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms: Medal awarding scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal shall be awarded annually to the artist of the most distinguished American picture book for children published by an American publisher in the United States in English during the preceding year. There are no limitations as to the character of the picture book except that the illustrations be original work. Honor books may be named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the core eligibility boundaries (American publisher/US publication/In English/original illustrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Illustrator citizenship/residency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal is restricted to artists who are citizens or residents of the United States. Books published in a U.S. territory or U.S. commonwealth are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who may receive the award (citizen or resident). Later Appendix B gives detailed definitions of 'resident' (e.g., green card, six months per year, permanent home).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Picture book for children'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'picture book for children' ... is one that essentially provides the child with a visual experience. A picture book has a collective unity of story-line, theme, or concept, developed through the series of pictures of which the book is comprised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes visual experience and unity of pictures as the central form; distinguishes picture books from other illustrated books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Child audience (age range)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'picture book for children' is one for which children are an intended potential audience. Children are defined as persons of ages up to and including fourteen and picture books for this entire age range are to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee should ask whether any 14-year-old would find the book suitable; books appealing to a narrow part of the range may still be eligible if exceptionally distinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Distinguished'
rubrics_metrics.description: “Distinguished” is defined as: Marked by eminence and distinction; noted for significant achievement. Marked by excellence in quality. Marked by conspicuous excellence or eminence. Individually distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these senses of 'distinguished' when judging works—eminence, excellence, conspicuous quality, individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Original work' (illustrations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'original work' ... defined as follows: The illustrations were created by this artist and no one else. The illustrations are presented here for the first time and have not been previously published elsewhere in any form. Illustrations reprinted or compiled from other sources are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality requirement applies to authorship and first publication of the illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'In English' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: “In English” means that the committee considers only books written and published in English. This requirement DOES NOT limit the use of words or phrases in another language where appropriate in context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only English-published books are eligible, but occasional use of other languages within the book is permitted; committee considers only the English text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Publication-year eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: “Published…during the preceding year” means that the book has a publication date in that year, was available for purchase in that year, and has a copyright date no later than that year. If a book is published prior to its year of copyright as stated in the book, it shall be considered in its year of copyright as stated in the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: every book eligible in one year only; avoid considering a book in more than one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: First-U.S.-publication / simultaneous publication
rubrics_metrics.description: “American picture book in the United States” means that books first published in previous years in other countries are not eligible. Books published simultaneously in the U.S. and another country may be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies ineligibility of works first published abroad prior to U.S. edition; simultaneous release is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluative criteria for 'distinguished' illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: In identifying a 'distinguished American picture book for children,' defined as illustration, committee members need to consider: Excellence of execution in the artistic technique employed; Excellence of pictorial interpretation of story, theme, or concept; Appropriateness of style of illustration to the story, theme or concept; Delineation of plot, theme, characters, setting, mood or information through the pictures; Excellence of presentation in recognition of a child audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five bullets are the core artistic criteria — evaluate craft, interpretation, stylistic fit, pictorial storytelling/communication, and child-focused presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form limitation / self-contained entity
rubrics_metrics.description: The only limitation to graphic form is that the form must be one which may be used in a picture book. The book must be a self-contained entity, not dependent on other media (i.e., sound, film or computer program) for its enjoyment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not award books that rely on external media to convey their value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of other book components
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee is to make its decision primarily on the illustration, but other components of a book are to be considered especially when they make a book less effective as a children’s picture book. Such other components might include the written text, the overall design of the book, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration is central, but text, design, typography, and layout may detract from or support the pictorial achievement and should be considered when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not criteria: didactic intent or popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee should keep in mind that the award is for distinguished illustrations in a picture book and for excellence of pictorial presentation for children. The award is not for didactic intent or for popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid awarding books merely for educational aims or commercial/popular success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational books: additional evaluation elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional considerations for informational books: Accuracy (author authority, currency, etc); Organization (appropriate scope and sequence); Documentation (appropriate citations to allow verification of facts); Clarity (delineation of fact and theory); Stimulating presentation of facts, concepts, and ideas; Features (index, table of contents, bibliography, glossary, graphics, author note, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a candidate is informational, apply these subject-specific quality checks in addition to pictorial criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child-audience suitability questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions for committees to consider include: Is there any 14-year-old for whom this book is suitable? If so, is it distinguished enough to be considered? If so, exactly what 14-year-olds would respond to it, and why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these probing questions to judge borderline age-suitability or books aimed at older youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'Resident' for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The author has established and maintains residence in the United States, U.S. territory, or U.S. commonwealth, as distinct from being a casual or occasional visitor, or the author meets one of the following criteria: a) the author, a citizen of another country, holds a “green card” and is a Permanent Resident Alien; b) the author lives for at least six months EVERY year in the United States; or c) the author’s permanent home is in the U.S., but the author is outside of the U.S. for a temporary purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives concrete residency tests and examples (e.g., green card holder, temporary abroad still eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: E-book / format exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: “Book” means the work was published in book format (pages between covers). Electronic books (e-books) and technological additions (including, but not limited to, CDs, DVDs, or accompanying websites) are specifically excluded from consideration of the book itself. A book published only in electronic format (e-book) is not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A later hardcover/paperback that follows an e-book initial publication is not eligible; accompanying media may exist but are not considered for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-published and small-press titles eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Books that are self-published or published by small presses are eligible, provided they meet all other eligibility requirements. Books are eligible in their first year of publication only. If a self-published book is republished later by another publisher, then the book will not be reconsidered upon its commercial publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair maintains list of self-published/small-press copies received; distribution to committee at Chair's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish book vs author/artist body of work
rubrics_metrics.description: The term, 'only the books eligible for the award,' specifies that the committee is not to consider the entire body of the work by an artist or whether the artist has previously won the award. The committee’s decision is to be made following deliberation about books of the specified calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must focus on the specific book under consideration, not past achievements or awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALSC Community Agreements for meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Community agreements outline best practices to ensure that everyone has an opportunity for expression, accountability, and growth: Speak for yourself; Embrace multiple perspectives; Be aware of privilege and oppression; Listen to and use people’s correct pronouns; Share the air; Interrupt attempts to derail; Acknowledge intent while addressing impact; Interrupt bias and take feedback; Remember opportunities to grow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these agreements to guide respectful, equity-minded committee discussion and to create space for inclusive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and award evaluation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusiveness is a core value... It is important that books demonstrate integrity and respect for all children’s lives and experiences and do not diminish or denigrate any individual or group through stereotypes, whitewashing, or other derogatory content. The committee should evaluate works with the consideration of all children in mind rather than privileging the dominant culture to the exclusion of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should be aware of personal biases, seek to listen and learn, and evaluate works for respectful, authentic representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest: definition and general duty
rubrics_metrics.description: A conflict of interest occurs when an individual's personal or private interests may lead an independent observer reasonably to question whether the individual's professional actions or decisions are influenced by considerations of significant personal or private interest, financial or otherwise. It is the policy... to ensure that members in all of its activities avoid conflicts of interest and the appearance of conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must proactively evaluate potential conflicts and consult leadership when in doubt; final decisions rest with the Executive Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific COI prohibitions for committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Members who have written or illustrated a book that may be eligible should not accept appointment; Members may not be employed by a children’s trade-book publisher, author, or illustrator; Members should not accept appointment if they have a close family or personal relationship with eligible authors/illustrators or with employees of a U.S. trade publisher; Members should not accept appointment if they or a close family member directly own equity representing more than a 5% stake in a U.S. trade publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete prohibitions help prevent actual or perceived conflicts; unresolved questions should be discussed with ALSC leadership before accepting appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members need to maintain a high degree of confidentiality regarding the committee’s discussions, both oral and written, in-person and virtual. Committee members may express only their own opinions and may not quote the opinions of other committee members or indicate in any way which titles are under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are encouraged to seek varied critical opinions but must avoid revealing committee deliberations or status of titles at any time; mock elections are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines on external communications and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may not engage in any print or electronic communication outside of the committee regarding eligible titles during their term of service... Prohibited communication includes professional/general journals, electronic discussion lists, blogs, and social-networking services. Members who write signed reviews must avoid publishing reviews of eligible materials during their term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After term ends, members may express personal opinions but must never reveal whether a title was under consideration or details of committee discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting attendance and access to materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons elected or appointed to an award committee should: Be able to attend all required discussion and decision meetings, in person and virtual; Have ready access to the major part of the current output of children’s books under consideration in outlets such as their local library or bookstore and through interlibrary loan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee membership presumes capacity for full participation; Chairs/Priority Group Consultant may assist in obtaining difficult-to-find titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of service restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: No individual may serve on the Batchelder Award, Caldecott Medal, Geisel Award, Newbery Medal, Sibert Medal, Children’s Literature Legacy Award, or Notable Children’s Books Committee more often than once every four years. The four-year period shall begin from the last year of the term of service regardless of length of term. This guideline will not apply to the appointment for Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits repeated service to preserve fairness and rotation of membership; emergency mid-year replacements may allow suspension of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with publishers: accepting books and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members may accept unsolicited books from publishers. The Chair consults members to verify addresses; the ALSC Awards Coordinator makes the committee roster available to publishers. Committee members are not to solicit publishers for free, personal copies of eligible books. Committee members should avoid conflicts of interest that might grow out of personal contact with publishing personnel. Members are not to solicit publishers for favors or invitations; unsolicited offers may be accepted only if they do not influence consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair/PGC coordinate requests for difficult titles; committee members must preserve impartiality in publisher interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher submission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit works for consideration for one of the ALSC awards, publishers should: Review the terms and criteria for the award. Submit one copy of the work to the award committee Chair. Publishers also have the option of sending a copy of the work to each committee member, but it is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline for submitting books is December 31 of the publication year; a list of committee members is available via Terms and Criteria page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note-taking / evaluation elements (sample form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample evaluation fields: Title/Author/Illustrator; Quality of Writing; Quality of Illustration (distinctive and engaging visual material, provides keys or clues to the text); Quality of Design (type size, spacing, white space, placement of illustrations); Style of presentation; For fiction: interpretation of theme/concept, plot, characters, setting, appropriateness of style; Child Audience (respect for children’s understanding, abilities, and appreciation up to and including age 14); Additional considerations for informational books (accuracy, organization, documentation, clarity, stimulating presentation, features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reminder: Not every book relies equally on every element; the book must be a self-contained entity; committee need not find excellence across the board but in elements relevant to the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books and post-selection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Honor books may be named. The artist may be awarded the medal posthumously. The committee is to consider only books eligible for the award as specified in the terms; decisions are made after deliberation about books of the specified calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures for naming honor books; notification and press release drafting procedures are in manual (e.g., notification calls prior to press conference).
